story.label: The Firm
story.title: We didn't set out to start a firm.
story.teaser: It began inside our own businesses — the messy, cross-cutting problems no single expert would own. We kept solving them, kept getting asked to do the same for others, and eventually said yes. That's all this is: a few people who are good at finding the problem everyone else walked past.

experts.label: The Experts
experts.title: A circle of experts we bring in when it helps.

ourStory.title: The help we wished we'd had.
ourStory.intro: Not a tidy origin story. The honest version is simpler: we kept hitting problems we couldn't solve alone, went looking for help, rarely found the kind we needed, and decided to become it.
body: Every one of us has hired the expert who was going to fix it, and watched it drift instead: the fix that ran long, cost more than the problem, and left the real trouble untouched. You explain what's wrong, they nod, and then they solve the version that fits what they already sell.

Rarely bad intent. A specialist sees deeply, but only down their own line, and many defend it hard, filing anything unfamiliar under a problem they've seen before. The symptom gets handled while the cause keeps working. And since it was never really their business, once it got heavy they had little reason to stay. Trust thins. It usually ends one way: you let them go, or you do it yourself.
Doing it yourself is no win. You have a company to run and a life to live. Becoming the reluctant expert on a problem you paid someone else to own is the opposite of what you needed.

What we learned is that the missing piece was never more expertise. It was the willingness to think past the brief, to sit on your side of the table, to keep pushing until it's actually done. That doesn't come with a qualification. It comes from putting your own money, name and sleep on the line, watching it fail, and finding a way through anyway.

That's who we are. Entrepreneurs and operators who have carried the weight, fallen badly, and climbed back. We know the loneliness of a problem that's yours alone, and the dread of watching it grow while the people you hired look away. So when we meet someone stuck in the same place, we can't quite leave them there. Not as a vendor selling hours, but as people who've stood where they're standing, turning back to help.
We do this because we know, first-hand, how much it matters to have someone who actually cares.

solutions.title: Two reasons people bring us in.
solutions.intro: There's no fixed menu of services. It usually comes down to one of two things — and the real problem is often deeper than the symptom that made you call.

repair.label: Repair
repair.body: Something's leaking — money, time, or quality — and what you've already tried hasn't worked. You need the real fault found, not the obvious one patched again.

boost.label: Boost
boost.body: The business works, but it isn't compounding the way it should. You want the next level, and a clear, honest route to reach it.

solutions.note: If you already know exactly what's broken and how to fix it, you don't need us.

engage.title: How it usually goes.
engage.intro: No contract up front, no sales dance. Here's how working together usually unfolds.
flow: It starts with a conversation. A call or a few messages, enough for each of us to get a feel for the other and what you're dealing with.

From there, we come to you. Sitting in your office, walking the floor and meeting your people tells us far more than any screen can, so we strongly prefer to visit in person. You cover the travel and stay, and in return we see the problem where it actually lives, which is rarely where everyone assumes. If an in-person visit truly isn't possible, we do this part online.

Then you get a preliminary read: what we think is really going on, and how we'd go about fixing it. If it feels right on both sides, that's when we agree the terms, with the problem finally in full view.
From there we get to work, and we see it through until the problem is actually solved.
engage.notesHeading: A few things worth stating plainly:
notes: The on-site visit is on your account: travel and stay, at cost. You can ask to keep it virtual, but a business is hard to read through a keyhole, and that tends to slow the fix or weaken it.
The engagement can be a one-time fee or a retainer, whichever fits the work and your preference.
If our preliminary read doesn't convince you, you owe us nothing and walk freely. No strings attached.
